candidates.title: KiF: Accelerating Low-Batch LLM Inference Using In-Flash KV Cache
candidates.abstract: Deploying LLMs on edge devices is constrained by the memory-intensive, dynamic KV cache. While offloading the KV cache to SSDs expands capacity, it introduces severe bandwidth bottlenecks. Existing in-flash processing (IFP) solutions, optimized for static weights, fail to address the write-intensive nature and access pattern mismatches inherent to the KV cache. We propose KiF, a novel IFP solution that manages KV cache within flash chips, via reliable pseudo-SLC based write management and specialized in-flash GEMV accelerator. KiF delivers up to 4.1× higher throughput than existing SSD offloading solutions.
candidates.reason: KiFはKVキャッシュをフラッシュチップ内で管理するインフラッシュ処理で、疑似SLC書き込み管理と専用GEMVアクセラレータによりSSDオフロードの帯域ボトルネックを解消し、低バッチLLM推論のスループットを最大4.1倍にするKVキャッシュ階層メモリの直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: DIAA: A Decoding-Efficient Inference Acceleration Approach for On-Device Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized intelligent interactions, enabling mobile applications such as personal assistants on edge devices for local execution. Speculative decoding (SD) has emerged as a promising paradigm to accelerate LLM inference without compromising generation quality, employing a draft-then-verify manner. However, due to the constrained computing and memory resources on edge devices, existing SD works heavily rely on an auxiliary draft model that incurs additional memory burden and hinders the adaptability, as well as static token trees that yield suboptimal inference performance. To this end, we propose DIAA, a Decoding-efficient Inference Acceleration Approach for on-device LLMs. DIAA achieves plug-and-play and model-agnostic inference speedup with memory and computation efficiency for edge devices. Specifically, a pair of lightweight look-up tables (LUTs) is constructed by Top-K token sampling to cache historical tokens and probabilities for rapid candidate drafting. DIAA integrates a dynamic token tree with prior LUTs enabling paralleled verification, updated during decoding process, to adapt the online context. A computation overlap is then employed to pipeline the update operations of token tree, LUTs, and KV cache to improve the computational efficiency. Finally, through extensive experiments implemented on edge platform NVIDIA Jetson, DIAA outperforms existing baselines in generation speed and inference wall-clock time, while incurring minimal memory overhead.
candidates.reason: DIAAはオンデバイスLLM向けに補助ドラフトモデルのメモリ負担と静的トークン木の非効率を解消する投機的デコード方式で、端末上のデコード高速化に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Efficient Pipeline Parallel Edge Inference for Large Language Models in Wireless Networks
candidates.venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
candidates.abstract: Edge computing enables distributed inference for computation-intensive applications. However, the autoregressive nature and large model size of large language models (LLMs) pose challenges for their deployment in wireless edge networks. Existing edge inference methods mainly assume an equivalent delay for each token generation step, which is inaccurate in practice. To address these challenges, we propose a pipeline parallel edge inference framework for LLMs, where tasks are grouped into multiple batches and processed in parallel by partitioning the LLM into multiple shards. An accurate latency model is established, where the latency of each token generation step increases during the autoregressive generation process. Building on this model, the end-to-end inference latency is minimized, which is formulated as a joint optimization problem of bandwidth allocation and model partitioning subject to heterogeneous GPU memory constraints. Then, we propose an efficient algorithm that derives a closed-form bandwidth allocation and design a dynamic programming algorithm for model partitioning. Extensive evaluations on BLOOM-3B and LLaMA-2-7B demonstrate that our approach reduces latency by up to 32.0% versus state-of-the-art baselines across diverse edge scenarios.
candidates.reason: 無線エッジネットワーク向けにLLMをシャード分割してパイプライン並列で推論する枠組みで、トークン生成ステップごとの遅延増を捉えた遅延モデルに基づきバッチ編成を行う、エッジLLM推論の直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: One-Step Limits of Randomized Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by proposing candidate continuations and verifying them in parallel. This letter studies a deliberately restricted one-step abstraction: under a parallel verification budget \(P\) , a non-anticipating policy proposes up to \(P\) continuations, and the accepted length is the longest verifier-consistent prefix. We show that, for any verifier prefix law and any deterministic or randomized policy, the probability of accepting at least \(\ell\) tokens is bounded by the top- \(P\) mass \(M_{P}(\ell)\) of the verifier's length- \(\ell\) prefix distribution. Consequently, \(\mathbb{E}[L_{P}]\leq\sum_{\ell\geq 1}M_{P}(\ell)\) . The result identifies covered verifier-prefix mass as the depthwise bottleneck in this one-step model: randomization cannot improve on the best deterministic prefix cover at any fixed prefix length. Under independent-token specializations, Rényi and collision-entropy bounds yield logarithmic-in- \(P\) limits, while uniform and spread-out regimes give matching or near-matching deterministic constructions. Stylized simulations and inference-only logits experiments illustrate the predicted diminishing returns.
candidates.reason: ランダム化投機的デコードの1ステップ抽象化のもとで、並列検証予算に対する受理トークン数の上限を検証器の接頭辞分布のトップ質量で与える理論結果で、投機的デコードの性能限界を定量化する直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
candidates.abstract: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) impose substantial KV cache demands from both large multimodal contexts and growing reasoning traces. Low-rank KV compression has emerged as a promising paradigm that stores low-dimensional latents of KV states and can be combined with quantization. However, existing low-rank methods often induce growing predictive policy drift from the dense model when compressing reasoning KV states, resulting in reasoning failures. We identify two key causes of this degradation: calibration-state mismatch between static contexts and on-policy reasoning states, and unequal error sensitivity across KV states. To address these challenges, we propose TraceKV, a training-free low-rank KV compression framework that unifies on-policy calibration, sensitivity-aware SVD, and global rank allocation under a single policy-preserving principle, substantially reducing policy-KL divergence during reasoning. Experiments across multiple VLMs and visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate superior accuracy--memory trade-offs, achieving near-lossless reasoning accuracy with 5.64$\times$ KV cache compression when combined with quantization. Optimized low-rank attention kernels further deliver up to 1.83$\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup. Code will be available at https://github.com/AK-DREAM/TraceKV.
candidates.reason: TraceKVは推論型視覚言語モデルのKV状態に対する低ランク圧縮で生じる方策ドリフトの原因を較正状態の不一致と誤差感度の不均一として特定し、方策を保つ圧縮を提案する、KVキャッシュ圧縮の直接の貢献である。
